participants.name: Maya
participants.bio: Architect, enthusiastic dinner host, and an unapologetic collector of very small bowls.

participants.name: Eli
participants.bio: Bookshop regular. Makes excellent pasta and has a wildly overambitious reading list.

participants.name: Theo
participants.bio: A designer who turns an ordinary Saturday into a very loosely planned adventure.

memories.text: I want a long-term relationship.
I want a monogamous relationship; we would agree before becoming exclusive.
I have room to date thoughtfully and can protect a couple of evenings a week to get to know someone.
I do not have children and want children eventually. I would share parenting responsibilities.
Meaningful work matters to me, but I protect evenings for a partner. During a demanding work week I would make a plan together and offer the same flexibility in return.
Separate accounts and proportional shared costs work for me; we each keep control of our personal spending.
I want affection and regular time together, with room for independent interests.
Our messages stay private. I can answer an honest question for reassurance, but I do not want either of us checking the other person’s phone.
I am not currently close with an ex. I am comfortable with a partner having an ex as a friend when boundaries and introductions are clear.
Close friendships matter. I want us both to keep time with our friends, and I can adjust plans for an important occasion without cutting people off.
I discuss disagreements directly, take a short break when heated, and agree on a time to come back to work it out.
If I hurt someone, I want to hear what landed badly, apologize for my part, and agree on something I will change. I expect the same willingness from a partner.
I am secular and do not need a partner to share a religion or attend religious services with me.
I can accept different beliefs if neither person pressures the other. I would object to either of us insulting people for their beliefs.
My mother may need to live with me; I have not yet explained what care I would expect a partner to provide.
If my mother needs care, I will arrange professional care and take responsibility for organizing it. I would not expect my partner to become her caregiver.
